slides.title: What's actually in a hotel price?
slides.body: The parts of the total, explained.

slides.title: The room rate.
slides.body: What the hotel charges for the room, the dates and the board you picked.

slides.title: Taxes.
slides.body: VAT or sales tax is usually in the total you see. The price breakdown shows it.

slides.title: City or tourist tax.
slides.body: Many cities charge it per person, per night. It's often paid at the hotel on arrival.

slides.title: Resort or facility fees.
slides.body: Some hotels add a daily fee for the pool, gym or wifi. Your booking details list it.

slides.title: A deposit at check-in.
slides.body: Some hotels hold a refundable amount on your card for extras. It's released after your stay.

slides.title: Our flat 10%.
slides.body: On Resapass it's already in the price you see. No booking fee added at checkout.

slides.title: 6 hotel location mistakes to avoid
slides.body: The map matters as much as the room.

slides.title: Trusting "centre" in the name.
slides.body: Check the real distance on a map. Names and descriptions can be generous.

slides.title: Ignoring the route from the station.
slides.body: Arriving late with luggage? Look at the walk from the station or airport first.

slides.title: Forgetting about hills.
slides.body: In some cities, a short distance can mean a steep climb. Street view helps.

slides.title: Booking above the nightlife.
slides.body: Light sleeper on a lively street? Read reviews for noise and ask for a quiet room.

slides.title: Missing the last ride back.
slides.body: Staying out of town? Check when the last train or bus runs to your hotel.

slides.title: Checking the hotel, not the area.
slides.body: Look for a supermarket, a pharmacy and somewhere to eat within a few minutes.

slides.title: Found the right spot?
slides.body: Compare hotels in that area on Resapass. Link in bio.

caption:
A great room in the wrong place can still ruin a trip.

Check the real distance, the route from the station, the hills, the noise, the last train back and what's around the hotel. Five minutes on the map saves a lot of walking.

slides.title: Barcelona: where to stay, by vibe
slides.body: 5 neighbourhoods, 5 very different trips.

slides.title: Gothic Quarter
slides.body: Medieval lanes, the cathedral and La Rambla a few steps away.

slides.title: El Born
slides.body: Narrow streets, the Picasso Museum and the church of Santa Maria del Mar.

slides.title: Eixample
slides.body: Wide avenues, Casa Batlló, La Pedrera and easy metro links.

slides.title: Gràcia
slides.body: Small squares, independent shops and a walk up to Park Güell.

slides.title: Barceloneta
slides.body: Seafood restaurants, the promenade and the sea at the end of the street.

slides.title: Forgot something? Ask reception first
slides.body: Things many hotels keep behind the desk.

slides.title: A plug adaptor or a charger.
slides.body: Many front desks keep adaptors and cables to lend. Ask before you buy one.

slides.title: A toothbrush or a razor.
slides.body: Forgotten toiletries are a classic. Hotels often have basic kits ready.

slides.title: An umbrella.
slides.body: Rain on day one? Some hotels lend umbrellas at the door.

slides.title: An iron or a steamer.
slides.body: Outfit for a meeting or a wedding? Ask for one instead of hunting for a shop.

slides.title: A different room.
slides.body: Noise from the street or the lift? Ask early in your stay, while rooms are free.

slides.title: Local tips.
slides.body: Staff know the bakery round the corner and where locals actually eat.
